--card: Follows --background, the editor canvas. VS Code uses upstream's panel.background only for its bottom panel: a darker step in Cyberpunk (#100d23 under #261d45), a near step in Umbra (#131341) and the canvas itself in Scarlet, so it marks no card surface.
--secondary: Upstream sets no secondary button color. Orca follows --muted, upstream's input.background.
--secondary-foreground: Upstream sets no secondary button color. Orca follows --foreground, upstream's workbench text.
--input: Follows --border. Upstream's input.border is the full mint accent in Cyberpunk and Umbra and a strong blue (#00a2ff) in Scarlet, which would put a strong color on every idle field. Orca shows a focused field with --ring, upstream's cursor color.
--chart-1: Upstream sets no charts.* color. Orca follows --primary, the style's accent button color.
--chart-2: Upstream sets no charts.* color, so the series keep Orca's built-in colors.
--chart-3: Upstream sets no charts.* color, so the series keep Orca's built-in colors.
--chart-4: Upstream sets no charts.* color, so the series keep Orca's built-in colors.
--chart-5: Upstream sets no charts.* color, so the series keep Orca's built-in colors.
--sidebar-primary: Follows --primary. Upstream has one button color for every view, the sidebar included.
--sidebar-primary-foreground: Follows --primary-foreground, upstream's button.foreground, for the same reason as --sidebar-primary.
--sidebar-accent: Follows --accent, upstream's editorSuggestWidget.selectedBackground, which the build checks is visible on the sidebar too. Upstream has one selected-row color for every list.
--sidebar-accent-foreground: Follows --accent-foreground, upstream's list.activeSelectionForeground, for the same reason as --sidebar-accent.
--sidebar-ring: Follows --ring, upstream's cursor color. Upstream has one focus color for every view.
--worktree-sidebar: Follows --sidebar. Upstream has one sidebar surface, sideBar.background, so the workspace list sits on it too.
--worktree-sidebar-foreground: Follows --sidebar-foreground, upstream's sideBar.foreground, because the workspace list is part of the one sidebar.
--worktree-sidebar-accent: Follows --sidebar-accent, upstream's list selection color on the sidebar.
--worktree-sidebar-active-border: Upstream sets no outline for the selected list row. Orca mixes 18% of the sidebar text into the sidebar border, a faint edge that keeps the row's selection fill as the main cue.
--chat-user-message: Upstream sets no chat color. Orca mixes the white text lightly into the chat canvas, which keeps the bubble in the canvas hue.
--chat-bold-foreground: Upstream sets no chat color. Orca follows the chat heading color, the white text, so bold text stays text and the accent stays for action and state.
--chat-inline-code: Upstream sets no textPreformat.background. Orca tints the chat canvas with the white text, which keeps the canvas hue.
--chat-inline-code-foreground: Upstream sets no textPreformat.foreground. Its curated Markdown inline code violet, #d57bff, reads 3.6:1 (Cyberpunk) and 4.4:1 (Scarlet) on Orca's inline code chip over the user message, and Cyberpunk's would leave the sRGB gamut before 4.5:1. So every style keeps Orca's own code text, the white text at 85%.
--chat-code-block: Upstream sets no textCodeBlock.background. Orca tints the chat canvas with the white text, which keeps the canvas hue.
--chat-selection-foreground: Follows --foreground, the white text upstream's selection shows.
--diff-added-gutter: Upstream sets no diffEditorGutter color, and VS Code then tints the diff gutter from the inserted color. Orca tints it from --diff-added the same way.
--diff-removed-gutter: Upstream sets no diffEditorGutter color, and VS Code then tints the diff gutter from the removed color. Orca tints it from --diff-removed the same way.
